root: ^Barnacle: Careful, traveler. Do not disturb the shelves. I sell herbs, tonics, and remedies, but each is potent,
^ and the powders — delicate… even dangerous if mishandled.

c-1: ^Barnacle: Of course. Every vial is brewed by my hand, beneath the ward of runes and moonlight.
^ One misstep could spoil the batch… or worse, invite a sickness best left unnamed.
^Barnacle: My ingredients come from marshes, caverns, and deep roots where fungi grow thick. Hazardous, yes — but powerful.
^ Untreated, they rot the lungs. Refined through alchemy, they mend the flesh, sharpen the senses… sometimes more.
c-2: ^Barnacle: As a child, I was frail. The fevers marked me, season after season. The healers whispered that I would not survive three summers.
^ But I did. And from that weakness grew my devotion to the study of disease and cure alike.
^Barnacle: I buried myself in books, in fire, in glass. Even now, I wake in the night certain that mold creeps unseen upon my walls.
^ Yet I do not flee that fear — I master it. I turn it into vigilance.

s0: ^Barnacle: Fenlora? A fine guardian. Yet fevers walk her halls more often than blades meet her foes. I remember each one.
s1: ^Barnacle: Aerandir tempers steel with sparks. Sparks fall to ash, and ash drifts into lungs. Few notice. I always do.
s2: ^Barnacle: Children wade in the river as if it were harmless. But water carries memory… and disease. I keep count.

c-4: ^Barnacle: Go with care. The world is never clean.
